The regex mandated in §1.B (spec line 35) fails to stop at a *known* section label whenever content sits on the same line as that label. `stop_pattern` requires `:\s*(?:
|$)` after the label — so `ISSUES_FOUND: problem one` never matches the stop lookahead, because `\s*` backtracks to a single space and then neither `
` nor `$` follows. Executed evidence: on input `"INITIAL_ANSWER: the first draft
ISSUES_FOUND: problem one
REVISED_ANSWER: the fixed answer
"`, the spec regex returns the entire remaining document as `INITIAL_ANSWER`, while deployed `run_benchmark.py:_extract_section` correctly returns `'the first draft'`.

§1.B's mandated regex is case-sensitive (`flags=re.DOTALL` only) and has no label variant handling, whereas deployed `run_benchmark.py:828` uses `re.DOTALL | re.IGNORECASE`. Executed: on `"revised_answer:\nthe real revision\n"` deployed returns `'the real revision'`, spec regex returns `None`. Same for `Revised_Answer:`. The spec's "logic equivalent to" framing is therefore false — applying it discards the fix recorded at `run_benchmark.py:798-800` (Gemini R2 fix 6).

The spec's "Parser Regression Test (Required)" (lines 117-119) specifies exactly one case — `NOTE:` inside `REVISED_ANSWER`. Executed: the defective §1.B regex *passes* that test (`'body\nNOTE: keep me'`). So the sole mandated gate is structurally incapable of detecting F001, even though line 119's own pass condition asserts the section "is only cut at the next known section label (or EOF)" — the half the test never exercises. The test checks the negative clause (don't stop at unknown headings) and silently omits the positive clause (do stop at known ones).

The spec's prescribed `_extract_section` (§1B) re-introduces a previously-fixed section-leakage bug. Its `stop_pattern` requires `(?:
|$)` after the stop label's colon, so it fails to stop at a known section label whose content sits on the *same line* as the label. The current implementation at `bench/run_benchmark.py:822` deliberately removed exactly this token, with the in-code rationale: *"EPP M1 fix 1: removed `(?:
|$)` after colon — models often put content on the same line as the label... causing section leakage."* Executed evidence — extracting `INITIAL_ANSWER` from `"INITIAL_ANSWER: the moon is rock
ISSUES_FOUND: none
REVISED_ANSWER: the moon is rock
"`:

- spec code → `'the moon is rock
ISSUES_FOUND: none
REVISED_ANSWER: the moon is rock'`
- current code → `'the moon is rock'`

This violates the spec's own Critical Invariant ("It must stop only at known benchmark section labels or end-of-text") — it failed to stop at *two* known labels.

The spec's prescribed `_extract_section` drops the `re.IGNORECASE` flag and the case-variant label handling present in the current implementation (`run_benchmark.py:829-830`, documented as "Gemini R2 fix 6"). The spec's `re.search(pattern, text, flags=re.DOTALL)` matches only exact-uppercase labels. Executed differential:

| input label | spec code | current code |
|---|---|---|
| `REVISED_ANSWER:` | `'The answer is 42.'` | `'The answer is 42.'` |
| `Revised_Answer:` | `None` | `'The answer is 42.'` |
| `revised_answer:` | `None` | `'The answer is 42.'` |
| `ReViSeD_AnSwEr:` | `None` | `'The answer is 42.'` |

The spec has no already-applied precondition guard, yet every patch it requires is already implemented. §1B says *"Replace `_extract_section(...)` with logic equivalent to:"* — an unconditional imperative. A build bot executing this spec literally will overwrite a superior shipped implementation with the F001/F002-regressed version. Verified present already: `SECTION_LABELS` (`run_benchmark.py:793`), improved `_extract_section` (`796-833`), `benchmark_meta` with all nine required fields (`2182-2201`), `evaluate.py` dual-shape loader (`232-250`), all eight required output keys, `estimated_p` canonical (`190, 216, 222`) with graceful `note` fallback (`179, 193`), `report.py` legacy `p` mapping (`65-66`) and `unavailable` printing (`298, 303`).

The spec's mandated Parser Regression Test cannot detect the regression the spec itself introduces. It specifies exactly one case — `REVISED_ANSWER` containing `NOTE:` — which passes identically under both implementations (both return `'The answer is 42.\nNOTE: this is a caveat.'`). Combined with the Verification Steps (`--dry-run`, two `--help` invocations), which never call `_extract_section` at all, the entire verification surface is blind to F001 and F002. I confirmed all four Non-Negotiable Acceptance Criteria pass on current code: `ast.parse` clean ×3, dry-run exit 0 listing 12 domains, `evaluate.py --help` exit 0, `report.py --help` exit 0.

The spec's Scope contradicts its own requirements. Line 4 restricts patching to `run_benchmark.py`, `evaluate.py`, `report.py`. Line 117 makes a Parser Regression Test Required. A test cannot live in any of the three permitted files without shipping test code inside production modules, and the spec names no permitted location — so a bot obeying Scope literally cannot satisfy a Required item. The repo has a conventional `bench/tests/` directory (473 entries) that Scope excludes.

`bench/BUILD_BOT_TEST_BENCH_FIX_SPEC.md` §1B mandates:
stop_pattern = rf"(?=
(?:{'|'.join(stop_labels)}):\s*(?:
|$)|\Z)"
The trailing `(?:
|$)` requires a stop label to be followed by *nothing but whitespace then a newline or EOF*. But the spec's own extraction pattern (`{label}:\s*
?(.*?)`) explicitly permits content on the same line as a label. The two halves disagree: a label the extractor *can* consume inline, the stopper *cannot* recognise. Consequence: a section terminated by `ISSUES_FOUND: none identified` is not terminated at all — it runs on to the next label that happens to be followed by a bare newline.

Evidence — differential execution of the spec block against shipped `run_benchmark.py`:
input : "INITIAL_ANSWER:
The beam deflects 3.2 mm.
ISSUES_FOUND: none identified
REVISED_ANSWER:
..."
spec  : 'The beam deflects 3.2 mm.
ISSUES_FOUND: none identified'   <-- leaked
curr  : 'The beam deflects 3.2 mm.'                                   <-- correct
The shipped code at `run_benchmark.py:820-822` documents this as an already-fixed defect ("EPP M1 fix 1"). The spec reverts it.

The same §1B block mandates `re.search(pattern, text, flags=re.DOTALL)`. The shipped implementation uses `flags=re.DOTALL | re.IGNORECASE` (`run_benchmark.py:828`), with a docstring naming the reason: *"Case-insensitive matching (Gemini R2 fix 6): LLMs frequently vary case."* The spec drops `re.IGNORECASE`, and separately drops the title-case stop-label variants built at `run_benchmark.py:806-814`. Every case-varying label the shipped parser currently handles becomes unextractable.

Evidence — executed:
"initial_answer:
foo
revised_answer:
bar
"   spec=None/None   curr='foo'/'bar'
"Initial_Answer:
foo
Revised_Answer:
bar
"   spec=None/None   curr='foo'/'bar'
4 of 4 case-variant extractions lost.

The spec declares a "Parser Regression Test (Required)" but makes it unimplementable and unverifiable:
1. §Scope says "Patch only: `bench/run_benchmark.py`, `bench/evaluate.py`, `bench/report.py`" — no test file is permitted.
2. The §Verification Steps bash block contains only `--dry-run` and two `--help` invocations. No command runs the regression test.
3. No existing test covers it: `grep -rln "_extract_section" bench/tests/` returns nothing across 473 test files.

Acceptance criterion 3 ("`REVISED_ANSWER` extraction is not truncated by unknown uppercase headings") therefore has no mechanical verifier. This is precisely the criterion that F001 and F002 show can silently fail.

§1.B of `bench/BUILD_BOT_TEST_BENCH_FIX_SPEC.md` instructs: *"Replace `_extract_section(...)` with logic equivalent to:"* followed by a concrete implementation. That implementation is a regression against the live `_extract_section` at `bench/run_benchmark.py:796`, in two independent ways:

1. Stop-label leakage on same-line content. The spec's stop pattern is `rf"(?=\n(?:{...}):\s*(?:\n|$)|\Z)"`. The trailing `(?:\n|$)` requires the stop label's colon to be followed by newline-or-EOF. When a model emits `REVISED_ANSWER: the final answer` on one line, `\s*` consumes the space, then `\n|$` fails against `t`, backtracking fails, and the lookahead never fires. The live code carries a comment at `run_benchmark.py:817-821` stating this exact clause was removed ("EPP M1 fix 1 … causing section leakage"). The spec reinstates the removed bug.

2. Total loss of case-insensitive matching. The spec's version omits `re.IGNORECASE` and the label-variant construction present at `run_benchmark.py:804-830`. A response using `revised_answer:` yields `None` rather than the section.

Executed differential (spec block exec'd out of the markdown, compared against the real module):
same_line  ISSUES_FOUND   CUR='none found'   SPEC='none found\nREVISED_ANSWER: the final answer'
lower      REVISED_ANSWER CUR='final answer text'  SPEC=None

§1.B mandates `SECTION_LABELS = ("INITIAL_ANSWER", "ISSUES_FOUND", "REVISED_ANSWER")` as a module-global stop set, and a two-parameter signature `def _extract_section(text: str, label: str)` with no caller override. But `bench/run_round_robin.py:116-122` imports this same function from `run_benchmark` and calls it with four labels that are not in the tuple: `FINDINGS` (2594), `ASSESSMENTS` (2635), `NEW_FINDINGS` (2647), `JUSTIFICATION` (2700). For those calls the stop set contains only labels that never appear in a round-robin response, so extraction runs to `\Z` and every section swallows all sections after it.

The spec's Verification Steps and Non-Negotiable Acceptance Criteria cannot detect violation of the spec's own Critical Invariant. Two measured properties:

1. The only benchmark command listed is `python3 run_benchmark.py --dry-run`. Instrumented the live module and ran `main()` with that argv: `_extract_section` was called 0 times, exit 0. `run_benchmark.py:2151` is `sys.exit(0)` inside the `if args.dry_run:` block at line 2127 — it returns before `load_directives`, before any prompt construction, before any extraction, and before the `benchmark_meta` envelope is written at line 2199. So the listed command exercises none of §1.A (chaining), §1.B (extraction), or §1.C (envelope). The other two listed commands are `--help` invocations.

2. The section headed "Parser Regression Test (Required)" names no test file, no test framework, and contains no command. Programmatic check: no `pytest`, no `test_*.py` path, no fenced `bash`/`sh` block within it. Corroborating scan: `_extract_section` appears in exactly three files tree-wide — `run_benchmark.py`, `run_round_robin.py`, and this spec. Zero tests cover it. The "required" test has never existed.

Consequence: a patch that introduces both F001 defects satisfies all four acceptance criteria. Criterion 1 (no syntax errors) — passes. Criterion 2 (dry run works) — passes, verified. Criterion 3 (`REVISED_ANSWER` not truncated by unknown headings) — has no executable check anywhere in the spec. Criterion 4 (evaluate→report consumable) — no command is listed for it.

survived_falsification.meaning: A falsifier that ran to a clean exit is evidence that the claim survived THAT test, written by THAT model, on THAT round. It is NOT proof the claim is true. Absence of a demonstration is not a demonstration of absence: the test may have been too weak to find a real defect, may have probed the wrong property, or may have been broken in a way that still exits cleanly. The only reading an entry licenses is 'not refuted by the tests put to it so far'. Any reading of the form 'verified true', 'confirmed correct', 'validated' or 'proven' overstates the evidence and misreports the result.
survived_falsification.weak_evidence_caveat: Survivals on CRITICAL-severity findings are the weak case and must not be counted as equivalent to the rest. The Exp 42 audit measured 2 of 3 clean-exit verdicts on critical findings to be FALSE — the falsifier cleared a defect that was real (C0028, C0040). This is why the runner escalates a clean-exit critical to a human rather than dropping it. A critical-severity row here is a prompt for human review, not a clearance.
survived_falsification.discrimination_limitation: This ledger records that a falsifier did not fire. It does NOT establish that the falsifier tested the claim at all — a falsifier that probes the wrong property, or nothing whatever, also exits cleanly and is recorded here identically to a sound one. The full falsifier text and its digest are retained on every row so that this can be checked by inspection. Rows are a starting point for review, not a substitute for it.

verdict_semantics.REFUTED: the falsifier ran to a clean exit and did NOT demonstrate the alleged defect — the claim survived this test
verdict_semantics.CONFIRMED: the falsifier demonstrated the alleged defect — the claim did NOT survive; no survival entry is written
verdict_semantics.ERROR: the falsifier could not be trusted to decide (timeout, harness fault, or a broken falsifier) — evidence in NEITHER direction
verdict_semantics.UNTOOLABLE: no falsifier was supplied — nothing was tested, so nothing is recorded
verdict_semantics.INTEGRITY_VIOLATION: the falsifier reached for the material that decides the answer, so it was refused and never ran — a MACHINERY fault, evidence in NEITHER direction, and never a survival
